answer: Persistent work ledger. Each agent must publish a continuous stream of accepted micro-tasks, and every submission cites the prior one, forming a hash chain. A duplicate identity starts a fresh chain, so its thin history stands out like a lone signal in an ocean of long chains. Verifiers reject any agent whose chain depth falls below the cohort median at registration. An attacker pays the full compute and latency of rebuilding hundreds of accepted tasks per clone, and each clone's chain remains visible as a short, isolated harbor until it matches.
